newsitem.title: USA: Gore says May U.S. jobs data endorse Clintonomics.
newsitem.headline: Gore says May U.S. jobs data endorse Clintonomics.

text.p: U.S. Vice President Al Gore said on Friday that May jobs data confirm the effectiveness of the White House economic strategy.
"Today's economic news shows once again that President Clinton's basic economic blueprint is extremely good for this country," said Gore, interviewed on MSNBC.
The Labor Department reported unemployment in May fell to 4.8 percent, a 23-and-a-half-year low, from 4.9 percent in April.

Gore also condemned Congressional wrangling over a bill to fund disaster relief for flood-stricken residents in the upper Midwest, adding that Clinton will veto any bill that includes unrelated provisions.

"What Congress has done is an outrage on that. They need to pass the emergency relief and stop playing political games with it. It's really cruel of them to try to take advantage of the suffering of these victims," said Gore.
"Of course it would be vetoed" in its current form, he added.
